source_text:
6 «οιδαμεν γάρ», φησὶν ̓Ιωάννης, «οτι οταν φανερωθῇ, ομοιοι αὐτῷ
ἐσόμεθα», καὶ Παῦλος τοὺς ἁγίους «συμμόρφους τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ» ἐκήρυξεν· πῶς
ουν τοὺς ἐν δόξῃ μέλλοντας φαιδρύνεσθαι ἁγίους ἐν ἀδόξῳ καὶ νεκρῷ καὶ ἀλάλῳ
θέλεις ὁρᾶν, τοῦ κυρίου λέγοντος περὶ αὐτῶν· «εσονται γάρ, φησίν, ὡς αγγελοι
θεοῦ». 7 πῶς δὲ καὶ ἀγγέλους πνεύματα ὑπάρχοντας καὶ ἀεὶ ζῶντας ἐν νεκροῖς
γράφων προσκυνεῖς, τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος «ὁ ποιῶν τοὺς ἀγγέλους αὐτοῦ
πνεύματα καὶ τοῦς λειτουργοὺς αὐτοῦ πῦρ φλέγον»; 8 λέγω δὲ ο τι οὐδὲ αὐτοὶ
θέλουσι προσκυνεῖσθαι.
9 «Ορα μή· σύνδουλος γάρ σου εἰμὶ καὶ τῶν ἀδελφῶν σου τῶν ἐχόντων τὴν
μαρτυρίαν Ιησοῦ. τῷ θεῷ, φησίν, προσκύνησον». 10 ἀλλ' οὐδὲ οἱ ἀπόστολοι
ἠθέλησαν προσκυνεῖσθαι.
thought_title: The saints' future glory makes images of them dishonoring
orientation: Epiphanius is arguing against making images of the saints, and here he cites John and Paul on the saints' future glory, then turns to the angels' refusal of worship.
pass_a_gloss: For John says, "We know that when he appears, we shall be like him," and Paul proclaimed the saints to be conformed to the Son of God. How then do you wish to see the saints who are about to shine in glory in inglorious and dead and voiceless matter, when the Lord says about them, "For they shall be, he says, like angels of God"? And how do you worship angels, who are spirits and always living, by painting them in dead things, when the prophet says, "He who makes his angels spirits and his ministers a flaming fire"? And I say that not even they themselves wish to be worshipped. "See that you do not; for I am a fellow servant with you and your brothers who hold the testimony of Jesus. Worship God," he says. But neither did the apostles wish to be worshipped.

choices.term: ἐν ἀδόξῳ καὶ νεκρῷ καὶ ἀλάλῳ
choices.english: in inglorious and dead and voiceless matter
choices.why: Keeps the three adjectives as parallel predicates of the material in which images are made, preserving the rhetorical contrast with the saints' glory.
rejected: in dishonorable and dead and speechless things

choices.why: Renders the future passive infinitive with its sense of radiant glorification, matching the contrast with inglorious matter.
Standard rendering for the angel's self-description in Revelation, preserving the compound's force.
Keeps the participial force of φλέγον as modifying πῦρ, matching the Septuagint wording.

choices.term: ὁ ποιῶν τοὺς ἀγγέλους αὐτοῦ πνεύματα
choices.english: He who makes his angels spirits
choices.why: Preserves the participial subject and the present tense of ποιῶν, matching the LXX citation.
rejected: the one making his angels winds

pass_b_english: John says, "We know that when he appears, we shall be like him" (1 John 3:2), and Paul proclaimed that the saints are "conformed to the Son of God" (Romans 8:29). So how can you wish to see the saints, who are destined to shine in glory, in inglorious, dead, and voiceless matter, when the Lord says of them, "They will be like the angels of God" (Matthew 22:30)? And how can you paint angels, who are spirits and always alive, painting them in dead things and worship them, when the prophet says, "He who makes his angels spirits and his ministers a flaming fire" (Psalm 103:4 LXX, 104:4 Hebrew)? I say that they themselves do not wish to be worshipped. "See that you do not do it; I am a fellow servant with you and your brothers who hold the testimony of Jesus. Worship God," he says (Revelation 19:10). But the apostles did not wish to be worshipped either.

problems.quote: in dead things and worship them
problems.why: γράφων means 'painting/drawing', not 'in dead things'; the deadness modifies the medium, not the location.
problems.fix: painting them in dead things and worship them
problems.ruling: γράφων is 'painting/drawing' (participle), not 'in dead things'; ἐν νεκροῖς modifies γράφων, meaning 'painting them in dead [matter]'

edits.old: in dead things and worship them
edits.new: painting them in dead things and worship them

problems.quote: I say that they themselves do not wish to be worshipped
problems.why: The 'I' is author, but 'they' shifts from angels to apostles without clear transition.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'The angels themselves do not wish...'

problems.quote: He who makes his angels spirits and his ministers a flaming fire
problems.why: Biblical quotation garbled: Hebrews 1:7/ Psalm 104:4 means God 'makes winds his messengers, flames his servants', not that angels are spirits.
problems.fix: Use standard translation: 'who makes his angels winds'.

edits.old: I say that they themselves do not wish to be worshipped.
edits.new: The angels themselves do not wish to be worshipped.

edits.old: He who makes his angels spirits and his ministers a flaming fire
edits.new: He who makes his angels winds and his ministers a flaming fire

fixed: Clarified 'they' to 'The angels' to avoid ambiguous shift to apostles.
Corrected 'spirits' to 'winds' in the Psalm quotation to match the source meaning.

problems.why: 'Inglorious' is odd for material substances; likely 'without glory' or 'ignoble' but applied to paint/plaster awkwardly.

problems.quote: "We know that when he appears, we shall be like him" (1 John 3:2)
problems.why: The quote matches 1 John 3:2, but the argument claims saints will be 'like the angels' (Matt 22:30)—yet 1 John says 'like him' (God/Christ), not like angels. The texts are conflated without acknowledgment.
problems.fix: Note the conflation or separate the citations.

problems.why: The 'he' could be the angel speaking or John reporting; unclear across the quote.
problems.fix: Specify 'the angel says' before the quotation.

problems.quote: He who makes his angels winds and his ministers a flaming fire
problems.why: Psalm 103:4 LXX is 'who makes his angels spirits'; 'winds' is the Hebrew rendering, not LXX.
problems.fix: Cite as Psalm 104:4 Hebrew or correct LXX wording to 'spirits.'

problems.quote: painting them in dead things and worship them
problems.why: Grammar breaks: 'painting...and worship' lacks parallel structure; reads like gloss.
problems.fix: Render as 'painting them in dead matter and worshipping them.'

edits.new: in base, dead, and voiceless matter

fixed: The 1 John 3:2 citation is correct as it stands; the source quotes John's words, and the argument about being like angels is a separate quotation from the Lord. No change needed.
The 'inglorious' issue is real; changed to 'base' to better convey the sense of material without glory.
The speaker issue is real; specified 'the angel says'.
The Psalm citation issue is real; corrected LXX wording to 'spirits'.
The grammar issue is real; changed to 'worshipping them'.

problems.quote: conformed to the Son of God
problems.why: Romans 8:29 reads 'conformed to the image of his Son', not 'to the Son of God'.
problems.fix: Quote accurately: 'conformed to the image of his Son'.

edits.old: conformed to the Son of God
edits.new: conformed to the image of his Son

fixed: The source reads συμμόρφους τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ, which literally means 'conformed to the Son of God.' However, the English adds a citation to Romans 8:29, and Romans 8:29 actually reads 'conformed to the image of his Son.' Since the English quotes Paul with a specific biblical citation, the quotation should match the cited verse. The source itself is a paraphrase, but the citation makes the mismatch a real problem. Fixed by changing the quoted words to match Romans 8:29.

last_rejected.why: English 'he says' hides that the angel is the speaker; source φησίν refers to the angel speaking, but brief marks angel as quoted speaker with implicit identification.
last_rejected.ruling: φησίν is standard 'he/she/it says'; implicit speaker identification is normal in such citations, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.source_quote: ἔσονται γάρ, φησίν, ὡς ἄγγελοι θεοῦ
last_rejected.why: The Lord's words 'They will be like the angels of God' are cited as Matthew 22:30, but brief says this 'echoes' Matthew 22:30 or Mark 12:25; however the source marks this as τοῦ κυρίου λέγοντος, and the citation may need checking. Actually Matthew 22:30 has 'ὡς ἄγγελοι' but not identical wording. Brief says 'echoes' not exact citation. The English adds a citation the source doesn't specify.
last_rejected.ruling: Source has no scripture reference; English adds standard citation for τοῦ κυρίου λέγοντος. Helpful identification, not a source error.
